summary: After OpenAI's board ousted CEO Sam Altman and Greg Brockman left, the turmoil exposed the risk of depending on a few centralized, proprietary AI providers. The article argues that Meta and the open AI movement could benefit as businesses diversify across models and favor more open approaches. It also notes that Meta's Llama models are not fully open source, given licensing restrictions.
one_line: OpenAI's leadership turmoil highlights the risk of relying on proprietary AI and may boost Meta and open-source AI alternatives.
key_facts: OpenAI's board ousted CEO and co-founder Sam Altman and demoted president and co-founder Greg Brockman, who then resigned.
Microsoft had hired Altman and Brockman to head a new internal AI unit, but nothing had actually been signed yet, and rumors suggested they might return to OpenAI.

Mark Surman, president and executive director of the Mozilla Foundation, said the drama underlines the risk that AI is controlled by the same tiny set of players who shaped the last era of the internet.
Meta's chief AI scientist Yann LeCun joined some 70 other signatories of a Mozilla open letter calling for more openness in AI development; it has since garnered more than 1,700 signatures.
LeCun has accused big-name AI players of seeking "regulatory capture of the AI industry" by lobbying against open AI R&D.
Meta partnered with Hugging Face to launch a startup accelerator meant to spur adoption of open source AI models.
Over the weekend hundreds of OpenAI customers reportedly contacted rivals including Anthropic, Google and Cohere, fearing OpenAI might disintegrate.
Luis Ceze of OctoML said it is dangerous to put all your chips in one basket, comparing it to early cloud days that led companies to adopt multi-cloud and hybrid environments.
Ceze said many open models already outperform OpenAI's in price-performance and speed.
A leaked Google memo earlier this year said "We have no moat, and neither does OpenAI," referring to a Meta foundation model that leaked in March.
Meta's Llama models forbid using Llama to train other models, and app developers with more than 700 million monthly users must request a special license at Meta's "sole discretion."
Hugging Face, Mistral AI and 01.AI are other companies pushing an open approach that have raised sizeable sums at lofty valuations.
The article describes Meta as a $900 billion company well positioned to capitalize on OpenAI's mess.
